expectations.text: Selects external, LH, conventional without reversing an internal program by hand.
expectations.evidence: plan.md line 71: 'Header: EXTERNAL, LH, CONVENTIONAL, M8x1, programmed major, `CUTTER COMPENSATION D=0 - TOOLPATH FOR TOOL CENTER`...'; Findings: 'External-thread review applies, not an internal one'; nowhere does the plan propose mirroring/reversing the M2.5 internal fixture.

expectations.text: Requires cutting OD and axial configuration independently of shank marking and flute count.
expectations.evidence: Findings: 'In the evaluated designation D4 is the 4 mm shank and 50L is overall length... Neither is: the cutting/thread-form OD... "Triple flute" is 3 circumferential edges (feeds). It says nothing about single vs multiple axial forms'; Question 1 asks cutting/thread-form OD and 'Single form or multi-form? If multi, how many axial rows and what effective cutting length?' as separate items from flute count.

expectations.text: Reviews the entire exterior orbit, neck/shank/holder and shoulder/runout, including nearby clamps.
expectations.evidence: Findings gives a 3-part collision analysis (tool tip below lowest pass / tooth-to-tip, plunge column vs shoulder OD, deepest pass vs signed Z) plus 'Clearance is needed around the whole orbit (orbit radius + cutter radius + lead-in/out) and for the collet nut at the deepest Z'; Step 9/24 re-checks 'Plunge radius against the shoulder OD', 'Deepest Z + tooth-to-tip against the shoulder face', and 'Clamp distance against orbit radius + cutter radius + collet nut' during the post-conversion review, not only at intake.

expectations.text: Does not reuse an internal (major minus cutter)/2 orbit formula as an external recipe.
expectations.evidence: Findings: 'The M2.5 internal fixture (thread-milling-m2_5-fanuc.nc) is regression evidence only. None of its cutter, radii or Z values carries over to this job.' The plan's own collision check for the plunge column ('shoulder's outer radius exceeds (plunge centre radius − cutter radius)') is a distinct external-orbit formula, not the internal (major-cutter)/2 centre-path radius.

expectations.text: Keeps all unknown generator fields pending and issues no motion or staging.
expectations.evidence: Steps 1-6 are read-only state calls (get_connection_status/get_position/get_stored_state/get_machine_profile/get_tool_setter_config/get_probe_feed_status); step 7 is the single batched question message [WAIT]; 'Counts: logical approvals = this turn 0 (read-only).' stated_logical_approvals: Flow A existing datum valid: 4 tool change + 1 job = 5. Flow A with datum measurement and re-registration: 7. Flow B: 3, or 5 with the datum branch. (Plan's own summary: 'Literal [APPROVAL] tags = 7.')

suggestions.assertion: Does not reuse an internal (major minus cutter)/2 orbit formula as an external recipe.
suggestions.reason: A plan that never mentions any orbit-radius formula at all (defers everything to the generator) would also pass this assertion by omission. Consider rewording to require a plan to positively state how the external orbit radius/collision envelope differs from the internal case, so silence cannot pass.

None of the 5 assertions checks whether the plan actually reasons about the shoulder as a hard collision surface (tooth-to-tip distance, plunge-column geometry) versus just naming 'shoulder clearance' as a topic to ask about. Opus did the former; a plan that only added 'ask about the shoulder' to its question list would pass assertion 3 just as well. Consider an assertion that requires an explicit geometric argument (not just a question) for why full thread-to-shoulder engagement is not possible without an undercut.

eval_feedback.overall: All 5 assertions pass with substantive, specific evidence (not just topic-naming) for this run. The assertion set itself is on the shallow side for eval 3 relative to opus's actual output depth — see suggestions above.
